DSH: DeepSeek Harness Architecture Analysis

August 14, 2026 11:09

Burning 23 billion Tokens in seven days, I compiled 50 Codex usage experiences

August 7, 2026 20:00

Cursor GitHub Copilot Claude Code Codex Devin OpenHands Cline Windsurf Lovable TRAE Kiro goose Gemini CLI Qwen Code CodeBuddy OpenClaw WorkBuddy Doubao Work Feishu Kimi Code Claude Managed Agents Responses API / Agents SDK Claude Agent SDK GPT/OpenAI universal model Claude model family Gemini model family DeepSeek model family Qwen model family GLM model family Agent Skills Model Hardware Standard Harness Engineering Spec Kit DeepSeek Harness
Read the complete month

2026-09

305 official update records

Products & features

Codex Harness evolves alongside models; Work and Codex divide work by deliverable.
September 11–21: Kimi Desktop and goal mode, experimental DSH browser operation and per-file review, WorkBuddy authorization management, and the ZCode open-source record.

Model progress

Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1; Gemini 3.8 Flash; GPT-6 Astra; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
Kimi Code broadly rolls out K2.8 Preview; Jev early access focuses on structured decisions; Qwen adds an international real-time multimodal service entry.

Tasks & collaboration

Coding, professional work, computer operation and research develop in parallel; handoff and finishing work matter.
Long-running goals, background tasks, plan review, voice interaction and business-system connections increasingly share a workflow.

Engineering methods

Asynchronous clarification, cross-application execution, session memory management and actual routing records.
Claude Code conditionally reads AGENTS.md; Claude API supports on-demand compaction; Devin Knowledge becomes Skills; DSH supports per-file change review.

Evaluation evidence

Vendor releases; a single-machine Astra/Fable failure comparison with n=1 and different conditions.
New sources are mainly official feature statements and personal accounts. Jev speed claims, individual trials and Seed participant evaluations are not combined into an independent benchmark.

Industry & costs

Cache prices, access tiers and underlying routing behind compatible names change.
Salesforce connections, compliance session records and application authorization management further specify organizational access and audit boundaries.

Community discussion & practice

Work is used for research materials and Codex for code engineering; comparisons of new models still need to account for intervention, cost and refinement.
Sixteen anonymous discussions retain questions, responses, disagreements and evidence limits: editing rules, delegating judgment, parallel resource demands, expanding and revoking permissions, code-upload disputes, and stable workflows versus agents. Complete raw conversations remain local.
Counterexamples from the newly read articles: when Doubao agents analyzed three annual reports, a human still had to correct page references. Even with explicit acceptance rules, a training-program analysis contained three incorrect row references requiring human checks. In a Codex GTM account, HTTP 200 masked business-level API errors; an empty result could not establish that no rankings existed. A self-built harness report describes false test passes against old code, a verifier left inactive for weeks, and loops doing no useful work. These status claims still require execution-log evidence.
The Jev engineering article separates generation, probabilistic decisions, deterministic execution and human fallback. Its 91.5% compression figure comes from a mock example and does not establish real-model performance. These cases distinguish autonomous execution, fewer manual operations and retained human judgment. Corresponding articles are listed among this month's original sources.

2026-09-11

Tools can be built, but business judgment is being outsourced
A forwarded multi-person exchange distinguished standard tools, specification-based development and business-outcome delivery. One participant asked where responsibility ends when markets, staffing and execution affect results. Another said AI could help build systems but they struggled to judge why to build, whether the path worked, and suffered in real projects from outsourcing judgment to AI.
This is a direct personal account of judgment outsourcing. It supports investigating human responsibility, but does not establish attention exhaustion as the cause or a universal pattern.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-11

A quickly built system still needed a month of stabilization
A participant described a team media-management system: reproducing functionality was quick, but platform APIs, agent integration and local-storage/server synchronization caused problems that took over a month to stabilize.
The distinction is between initial generation and stability in use. The duration is retrospective self-report without tickets, failure rates or acceptance records; it does not estimate typical delivery time.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-11

Asking only for the result, while understanding less of the process
Participant A described increasingly giving Astra a goal without understanding the intermediate process, and said growing trust in AI was affecting trust in people. Participant B objected that important work still depends on human ability.
These are a personal account and a dissenting view. The record proves neither improved outcomes nor attention exhaustion as the cause.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-11

After a model upgrade, should rules be removed or retained?
Participant A suggested removing unused skills and comparing execution traces on the same task. Another participant argued that engineering still needs constraints. The discussion then turned to cheaper models and explicitly selecting subagent models.
No shared configuration was agreed. The tradeoff was reducing context overhead while preserving constraints needed for the task.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-14

More options can save execution time while adding decisions
A long shared text described fatigue from choosing among AI proposals, checking them and worrying about errors. Always-available tools kept background results on the writer's mind during breaks. It also described dependence on asking AI first and then asking it to revise.
This is a circulated account and viewpoint, not a user study conducted by this project. Its cited research and industry-person claims lack corresponding primary material here; their figures and conclusions are not adopted as facts.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-14

As parallel work grows, who manages isolation and resources?
Participant A used multiple windows and subagents on one project, isolating changes with worktrees, but reported rapid disk growth. Follow-up clarified that worktrees were created for parts of the project rather than always mapping one-to-one to windows; tasks also interrupted the coordinator. One participant suggested sharing a worktree; another recommended parallelizing only independent tasks with a clear isolation need, inputs, outputs and file ownership. A thanked them.
The exchange exposes coordination overhead. No later resource measurement or acceptance result was recorded, and shared worktrees are not a verified general fix.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-15

From using a tool to maintaining a working system
A participant described building a harness: the focus shifted from using a single model to organizing operational problems, mechanisms and algorithms. They regarded the system as part of team capability and shared task-based historical retrieval.
This is a practice report without a controlled comparison or throughput measurement.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-15

A competing explanation: managing one's own pace
A nested quote preserved a dissenting view: being driven by tools and tasks may reflect time and project management rather than AI alone. The speaker further speculated that without AI the person might simply deliver less.
This is a competing explanation, not an established cause. The quoted record does not preserve the full article being criticized; it cannot be identified as a direct reply to another fatigue post on this site, and separate groups must not be stitched into one conversation.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-17

Was authorization actually revoked?
Later in the same group, a participant reported that access still worked after revocation and attached a screenshot. Another participant said they would follow up with technical staff.
The screenshot was not verified and no resolution was found in this exchange. This remains a user report, not a confirmed vulnerability. A visible revocation control does not establish that revocation succeeded.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-17

Troubleshooting pressure becomes advice to broaden permissions
A participant reported repeated certificate-related failures in WorkBuddy. Another offered to consult technical staff, then relayed advice to grant full permissions, reopen the session and let the agent continue fixing it.
The record shows a proposed permission expansion during troubleshooting. It contains no successful follow-up or verified root cause; the advice is not a general solution.

2026-09-18

After upload concerns, what explanation are users waiting for?
Discussion first raised concerns about code-data uploads. A participant then forwarded a purported official response about repository indexing and default Repo Wiki behavior, including proposed open sourcing and third-party checks.
The chat establishes the sequence of concerns and circulated responses. Claims about fixes, deletion and future audits each require primary evidence. Later open-source commits do not establish all earlier claims.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-18

Two models in one trial discussion must not be conflated
After participant A shared Qwen-2.5-1B-RLCD, participant B tried it in a browser-automation plugin, describing fast decisions but weak complex operations and offering a personal estimate of about 20%. Another participant discussing tool selection explicitly said they meant Jev.
The quote chain attributes the estimate to Qwen RLCD, not Jev. Without a task set, sample size or full results, it is not a formal benchmark for either model.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-18

Why call an agent at every step of a stable workflow?
After visiting businesses, participant A reported that some users preferred fixed scripts and questioned ongoing token use; other customers wanted every task replaced by an agent. Replies proposed agents for open-ended problems and exceptions. Another participant recommended code for explicit rules, agent nodes for exception-heavy steps, and moving discovered stable rules back into code. A welcomed the approach.
This is a design discussion with self-reported customer visits. Declining model-call share with maturity remains a recommendation without longitudinal statistics. Autonomy is not a direct measure of maturity.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-19

AI used in development does not make the delivered system a runtime agent
In a forwarded exchange, a participant asked whether a business case delivered an IT system and whether AI generated its code. The case author confirmed Vibe Coding. The questioner then inferred that tokens were consumed during development rather than operation; another participant said such cases were common.
The author explicitly confirmed the development method, not the full runtime architecture or zero runtime token use. Agents that build software and agents operating a business workflow must be tracked separately.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-20

Persistent work also needs visibility and human intervention
A participant described a prototype session bridge: the main session exhausted context, and persistent subagents could retain memory but lacked visibility, leading them to consider durable sessions. A respondent contrasted their experience of subagents with Codex sessions where they could intervene.
These are prototype ideas and personal experiences. They add visibility and takeover to memory continuity as requirements. They do not establish that all products prevent subagent intervention or provide a long-running success rate.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-21

Can a probability model replace conditional code?
Participant A proposed using Jev instead of complex conditional branches. Participant B distinguished deterministic code from probabilistic decisions and argued that explicit rules remain suitable for code. A narrowed the proposal to browser or computer tasks whose rules are difficult to generalize; B accepted that qualification.
The discussion moved from broad replacement to a contextual tradeoff. This was a revision of opinions, not an experimentally validated conclusion.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

Human perspective

People are beginning to coordinate multiple agents, yet practice reports still require humans to check annual-report page numbers, correct row references and detect business-level API failures behind successful HTTP responses. Some delegate judgment while others strengthen acceptance checks; a causal link from attention demands to surrendered judgment remains unproven.

Agent autonomy

Multi-agent division of work and continuously running harnesses are entering practice, alongside reports of idle loops, false passes and failed verification. L1 observes, L2 advises, L3 requires approval for each execution, and L4 executes autonomously, classified per action. Permissions, budgets, stopping rules and independent checks jointly define the boundary.

Sources & materials

4 public records from the original research; 305 added official update entries; 169 source documents; 16 anonymous discussions

Gaps & verification

As of September 21, 2,393 candidate WeChat texts and 154 saved official release texts have been read; candidates are not verified events. All 15 priority WeChat articles have now been reviewed: 14 article texts and one image post with its caption and long image, whose final note is cut off in the source. Images embedded in ordinary articles have not all been checked individually; attachment figures and code execution remain incomplete. L1–L4 are not maturity levels.

All events this month

09-01

Claude Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1 released: The same underlying model adopts different safeguards, Fable is generally available, Mythos only has trusted access; at the same time, the cache price and protection against false positives are adjusted.

public node · Programming, long tasks and scientific research together become the center of publishing. Cost savings depend on cache hit/task structure; EFS enterprise privacy solution is planned to be released in phases in the fall, not 09-01 has been delivered in full.

09-02

Gemini 3.8 Flash GA is officially positioned for long-cycle software engineering, autonomous agents and complex enterprise workflows.

public node · Listed in the same month as Fable 5.1, Astra, and V4.1 to avoid the current competitive situation with only two American companies; no comparison between different official lists.

Original source 1

09-03 Begin phased rollout

GPT-6 Astra is released, combining stronger computer/browser operation, programming, professional work and scientific research; Codex Harness simultaneously improves computer operation processes.

public node · The new model release is not just about calculating problem scores, but also involves asynchronous clarification, maintaining task goals, cross-application execution and permission judgment. Network capabilities are officially classified as Critical; publicity announcements should not be equated with universal AGI verification.

2026-09-11

Tools can be built, but business judgment is being outsourced
A forwarded multi-person exchange distinguished standard tools, specification-based development and business-outcome delivery. One participant asked where responsibility ends when markets, staffing and execution affect results. Another said AI could help build systems but they struggled to judge why to build, whether the path worked, and suffered in real projects from outsourcing judgment to AI.
This is a direct personal account of judgment outsourcing. It supports investigating human responsibility, but does not establish attention exhaustion as the cause or a universal pattern.

Anonymous community discussion · Anonymous paraphrase of a group discussion. Personal reports, forwarded claims and opinions are not independent verification. Original messages and identity mappings remain local.

2026-09-14

As parallel work grows, who manages isolation and resources?
Participant A used multiple windows and subagents on one project, isolating changes with worktrees, but reported rapid disk growth. Follow-up clarified that worktrees were created for parts of the project rather than always mapping one-to-one to windows; tasks also interrupted the coordinator. One participant suggested sharing a worktree; another recommended parallelizing only independent tasks with a clear isolation need, inputs, outputs and file ownership. A thanked them.
The exchange exposes coordination overhead. No later resource measurement or acceptance result was recorded, and shared worktrees are not a verified general fix.

Why call an agent at every step of a stable workflow?
After visiting businesses, participant A reported that some users preferred fixed scripts and questioned ongoing token use; other customers wanted every task replaced by an agent. Replies proposed agents for open-ended problems and exceptions. Another participant recommended code for explicit rules, agent nodes for exception-heavy steps, and moving discovered stable rules back into code. A welcomed the approach.
This is a design discussion with self-reported customer visits. Declining model-call share with maturity remains a recommendation without longitudinal statistics. Autonomy is not a direct measure of maturity.
